name: Snapshot State Manager
description: Manage engine state checkpoints for quick recovery and comparison. Save, load, list, compare, and clean engine state snapshots captured via StateSnapshotAdapter. Essential for CI/CD workflows, regression testing, and before/after feature validation.
author: cargo-cicd maintainers

list.name: list
list.description: Display all saved engine state snapshots with metadata

verbose.description: Show full snapshot contents including changed files and stage records

default.format: Plain text table with columns: Name, Timestamp, Workspace Root, Toolchain, Changed Files, Size, Schema Version

verbose.format: Full YAML or formatted text with all fields expanded
verbose.example:
Snapshot: snapshot-main-2024-01-15-143022
  Created: 2024-01-15 14:30:22
  Workspace Root: /home/user/cargo-cicd
  Toolchain: stable (1.75.0)
  Changed Files: [src/lib.rs, src/adapters/state_snapshot.rs, tests/cli.rs]
  Target Bytes: 523,890,432 (500 MB)
  Git Phase: dirty (ahead 3 commits)
  Stages: build (✓ 2345ms), test (✓ 5678ms), publish (✗ failure)
  Schema Version: 1

use_cases: Review saved state checkpoints before deciding which to restore
Track snapshot history over time to identify trends or regressions
Audit what state was captured at each checkpoint

save.name: save
save.description: Force a snapshot save with an optional label or auto-generated timestamp

label.description: Descriptive label for the snapshot (e.g., 'pre-refactor', 'stable-build'). If not provided, auto-generates timestamp-based name like 'snapshot-2024-01-15-143022'.

success.format: Plain text confirmation with snapshot name and path
success.example:
✓ Snapshot saved: snapshot-pre-feature-x
  Location: /home/user/cargo-cicd/.cargo/cicd_state.snapshot
  Size: 2.4 KB
  Timestamp: 2024-01-15 14:30:22

error.example: ✗ Failed to save snapshot: Permission denied writing to .cargo/cicd_state.snapshot

use_cases: Checkpoint state before attempting risky refactors or major changes
Create baseline snapshots for regression testing
Save state at known good points in CI/CD pipeline for later recovery
Track before/after state for feature flag experiments

load.name: load
load.description: Restore engine state from a saved snapshot back into the workspace

snapshot_name.description: Name or path of the snapshot to restore. Can be a short name (matched from .cargo/cicd_snapshots/) or full path.

force.description: Skip confirmation prompt and force restore even if current state has uncommitted changes

backup.description: Save current engine state to backup before restoring snapshot

confirmation_prompt.description: Prompt user to confirm state restore
confirmation_prompt.example:
Restore from snapshot 'snapshot-pre-feature-x'?
  Current workspace root: /home/user/cargo-cicd
  Restore toolchain: stable → stable-1.79.0
  Restore changed files: 3 files → 5 files
  Git phase: dirty → clean

  Backup current state? [y/N]:

success.example:
✓ State restored from snapshot 'snapshot-pre-feature-x'
  Workspace: /home/user/cargo-cicd
  Toolchain: stable-1.79.0
  Changed Files: 5 files (src/lib.rs, src/adapters/state_snapshot.rs, ...)
  Backup saved to: .cargo/cicd_state.snapshot.backup-2024-01-15-143022

use_cases: Quickly revert to a known good state after failed experiment
Restore workspace state from CI/CD run for local reproduction
Jump between regression baselines for comparative testing

compare.name: compare
compare.description: Diff two snapshots to identify what changed between them

snapshot1.description: Name or path of first snapshot (baseline for comparison)

snapshot2.description: Name or path of second snapshot (compared against baseline)

text.format: Organized by state dimension with color-coded changes
text.example:
Workspace State:
  root: /home/user/cargo-cicd (unchanged)
  name: cargo-cicd (unchanged)

Toolchain State:
  active: stable → stable-1.79.0 [CHANGED]
  rust_version: 1.75.0 → 1.79.0 [CHANGED]
  override_path: (none) → /usr/local/rust [ADDED]

Changed Files:
  [REMOVED] src/workspace/snapshot.rs
  [ADDED] src/adapters/state_snapshot.rs
  [ADDED] tests/invariants.rs
  [MODIFIED] src/lib.rs

Target State:
  target_bytes: 500 MB → 523 MB [CHANGED]
  build_cache: 45% → 52% [CHANGED]

Git Phase State:
  phase: dirty → clean [CHANGED]
  commits_ahead: 3 → 0 [CHANGED]
  modified_files: 5 → 0 [CHANGED]

Test Plan:
  total_tests: 45 → 48 [CHANGED]
  skipped: 2 → 0 [CHANGED]

Stage Records (timing changes):
  build: 2345ms → 2198ms [-147ms, 6.3% faster]
  test: 5678ms → 6234ms [+556ms, 9.8% slower]
  publish: FAILED → SUCCESS [STATUS CHANGE]

json.format: Structured JSON with from/to values for each changed field

diff.example:
--- snapshot-pre-feature-x
+++ snapshot-post-feature-x
@@ Toolchain @@
-active: stable
+active: stable-1.79.0
@@ Changed Files @@
-src/workspace/snapshot.rs
+src/adapters/state_snapshot.rs

csv.format: Field, Snapshot1, Snapshot2, Change Type, Details

use_cases: Quantify impact of a refactor or feature on workspace/toolchain state
Identify unexpected side-effects (e.g., extra changed files after a 'simple' PR)
Track build time or test suite size changes across regression baselines
Generate reports showing before/after of CI/CD runs for audit or review
Detect toolchain drift or build cache degradation over time

clean.name: clean
clean.description: Remove old snapshots beyond a specified retention count

keep_count.description: Number of most recent snapshots to retain. Older snapshots are deleted. Default 5.

older_than.description: Delete snapshots older than this many days. If both --keep and --older-than are specified, delete if EITHER condition is met.

dry_run.description: Show which snapshots would be deleted without actually deleting them

dry_run_output.description: List of snapshots that would be deleted
dry_run_output.format: Numbered list with snapshot name, age, and size
dry_run_output.example:
Dry run: would delete 3 snapshots, freeing 7.8 MB

  1. snapshot-old-baseline (89 days old) - 2.4 KB
  2. snapshot-feature-x-v1 (45 days old) - 1.8 KB
  3. snapshot-regression-2023-11-01 (31 days old) - 3.6 KB

Retained snapshots (5 most recent):
  ✓ snapshot-main-2024-01-15-143022 (0 days old)
  ✓ snapshot-pre-merge-fix (3 days old)
  ✓ snapshot-stable-v1.0 (7 days old)
  ✓ snapshot-feature-y (14 days old)
  ✓ snapshot-production-baseline (21 days old)

success.example:
✓ Cleaned up snapshots
  Deleted: 3 snapshots
  Space freed: 7.8 MB
  Retained: 5 snapshots
  Total remaining size: 12.4 KB

use_cases: Prevent snapshot directory from consuming excessive disk space
Maintain a rolling window of regression baselines (e.g., keep last 5)
Archive old snapshots by deleting those older than a date threshold
Cleanup after completing a feature branch or experiment

before_refactor.title: Before/After Refactor Comparison
before_refactor.description: Snapshot before a major refactor, make changes, then compare to quantify impact
before_refactor.use_case: Verify that refactor didn't introduce unexpected side-effects like extra changed files or build time regression

regression_baseline.title: Regression Testing with Baselines
regression_baseline.description: Establish known-good baseline snapshots and jump between them for testing
steps: # On feature branch: test against baseline
snapshot-state-manager compare snapshot-stable-v1.0 snapshot-current --format json > regression-report.json
regression_baseline.use_case: Detect regressions by comparing feature branch state to a known-good production baseline

ci_cd_recovery.title: CI/CD Failure Recovery
ci_cd_recovery.description: Save state at pipeline checkpoints, restore if later stage fails
steps: # Step 2: publish stage fails for some reason
# Developer reproduces locally by restoring checkpoint
# Now developer can debug publish stage in exact CI state
ci_cd_recovery.use_case: Reproduce CI/CD environment and state locally for debugging without re-running full pipeline

feature_flag_experiment.title: Feature Flag A/B Testing
feature_flag_experiment.description: Compare state with different feature flags enabled/disabled
feature_flag_experiment.use_case: Quantify the cost/benefit of a feature flag: what files change, does toolchain shift, does build time increase?

snapshot_structure.description: Internal structure of stored engine state snapshots

fields.changed_files: List of Rust source files detected as changed relative to workspace root
fields.target_bytes: Total bytes occupied by target/ directory (cache footprint)
fields.git_phase: Current git status label (e.g., clean, dirty, ahead, behind)
fields.schema_version: Version of snapshot format (for forward compatibility)
fields.stages: Array of per-stage timing and outcome records {name, ok, elapsed_ms}

integration.feature_flag: advanced — required to enable snapshot functionality
integration.storage: Uses Rust bitcode serialization for compact storage

error_handling.snapshot_not_found: If snapshot name doesn't exist, list available snapshots and suggest matches
error_handling.permissions_denied: If unable to write/read snapshots, explain required .cargo/ directory permissions
error_handling.schema_mismatch: If loading snapshot with incompatible schema version, show schema version in snapshot and current version, offer upgrade path
error_handling.corrupt_snapshot: If bitcode decode fails, show file path and size, suggest deleting and re-saving
error_handling.disk_full: If unable to save due to disk space, show required space and current free space on volume

safety_features.no_destructive_load: Loading snapshot does not overwrite workspace files; it only restores EngineState metadata. User files remain untouched.
safety_features.backup_on_load: By default, saves current state to .backup file before loading snapshot (--backup flag)
safety_features.dry_run_on_clean: Clean command supports --dry-run to preview deletions before committing
safety_features.confirmation_prompts: Interactive confirmation before destructive operations (load, clean)
safety_features.immutable_snapshots: Snapshots are read-only; compare and list operate safely without modifying stored data

performance_notes.encoding: Bitcode is ~5-10x more compact than JSON for typical engine state
performance_notes.io_bound: Snapshot I/O is bounded by disk speed; compare operations are CPU-bound (diff computation)
performance_notes.scalability: Snapshot size grows with number of changed files and stages tracked; typically 1-5 KB per snapshot
